analysis:
This PR changes documentation only. In docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (line 97), the PR adds a note that the gpt-oss-20b 3.5 GiB measured activation floor was measured while activations were float32 after layer 0, and has not been re-measured with bf16 activations. In docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1163), the PR adds a note that a bf16 gpt_oss checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamps with dtype-typed scalars (GPTOSS+Experts.swift swiglu).

No source code, gates, cache scoping, encryption or authorization behavior changed in the supplied units. Prefix-cache claims are unchanged, including cache-scope partitioning, SSD tier HMAC tags and the T-041/SEC-035 posture. Attestation and serving authorization (TB-011, T-053/T-054) are not touched.

The documented dtype change implies the KV layout and dtype for gpt-oss may differ from earlier float32 K/V. That could affect existing SSD/complete-checkpoint compatibility. The threat model says layoutEpoch and observed dtype gates fail closed, so mismatched payloads are rejected rather than misused. The SwiGLU code itself is outside the supplied evidence.

The unmeasured activation floor is an availability/memory-accounting accuracy question (T-029/T-016 adjacent), not a confidentiality regression. If integration sees the corresponding Swift change to GPTOSS+Experts.swift or to the floor constants, it should verify two things: that the dtype gates and layout epoch for historical checkpoints reject float32-era SSD entries, and that the 3.5 GiB floor remains sufficient. No security regression was identified in these doc units.
